open_issues: Core Arabic strings for this package went into a new src/Wakeel.Core/Services/Correspondence/LetterAr.cs instead of CoreAr.cs. CoreAr.cs is outside the paths I was given (Core was limited to Services/Correspondence interfaces + TemplateService) and is being edited concurrently by another package (it shows as modified in git status), so appending to it risked a lost edit. LetterAr is documented as the letter package's slice of the same idea and follows the same shape; merging it into CoreAr is a straight append if the supervisor prefers one file.

tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests.csproj gained a ProjectReference to src/Wakeel.Reports (required: adding a Wakeel.Reports.Tests project to Wakeel.slnx is forbidden, and the letter tests must reference the composer). src/Wakeel.Reports/Wakeel.Reports.csproj gained one EmbeddedResource (the approved reference docx, embedded from its own docs/ path so the shipped default cannot drift), and src/Wakeel.Reports/Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs an InternalsVisibleTo for the test assembly. No new NuGet package was added; Directory.Build.props, Directory.Packages.props, Wakeel.slnx and docs/ (except the progress file) were not touched.

The late-bound Word COM engine sits in src/Wakeel.Reports/Letters/WordSession.cs rather than entirely in Wakeel.Desktop. Wakeel.Desktop is a net10.0-windows WPF exe that a net10.0 test project cannot reference, and the spec requires a Word test that runs when Word is present. src/Wakeel.Desktop/Services/WordAutomation.cs still holds the Desktop-facing behaviour the spec names (staging file, open, wait for close, import the changes, «Word غير متوفر», plus EditFileAsync for W88's «فتح قالب المراسلة في Word»); only the COM calls live in the class library.

LetterPdfWriter's WebView2 fallback (PrintToPdf on the letter's HTML) is wired, registered and compiles, but has no automated test: it needs a live CoreWebView2 from the running window, which no test project here can create. The Word path it prefers is tested end to end, and the HTML it prints is tested on its own (no placeholder text anywhere on the page, A4/A5 page size, lists, bold, escaping, RTL isolation).

The 'will the referral fit at the foot of the last page?' answer is an estimate (LetterPageFit), not a Word layout: الوكيل must answer before the user saves and without Word installed, so it counts lines from the writing area and the paragraph's font size. It is tuned to read slightly pessimistically — a referral pushed onto its own page costs a sheet of paper, one that overflows the page it was promised costs a reprint of an official document. Worth calibrating against a few real printed letters during the B3 walkthrough.

Numbered and bulleted lists use real numbering definitions added to the generated document, which is only possible in the main document part. If an office's template ever placed @نص المراسلة inside a header or footer, the markers fall back to literal text. Nothing in the reference template does this.

Building src/Wakeel.Desktop was blocked four times by MSB3027/MSB3021 file locks — a running Wakeel.Desktop.exe (another agent's) held Wakeel.Core.dll and Wakeel.UI.dll in its output folder. The C# compilation was clean throughout, and the full build succeeded on retry; the final run of every command in the package's build/test line is green.
notes:
Conformance is the headline result. Composing from docs/templates/correspondence/نموذج-المراسلة.docx with the owner's own values produces text identical, paragraph for paragraph, to his hand-filled مثال-مراسلة-المالك.docx (LetterConformanceTests.Generated_letter_reads_the_same_as_the_owner_s_filled_example). His hand-written «19 صفر 1448» and «2 أغسطس 2026» are the independent ground truth the UmAlQuraCalendar conversion and both sets of Arabic month names are asserted against. The Word COM test ran for real on this machine: the composed letter became a non-empty PDF and no WINWORD process was left behind. 88 of the 566 passing tests are this package's.

Design decisions. (1) Mark replacement never looks at a single run: each paragraph's text nodes are read as one string with an index back to the node holding each character, the mark is found there, and the replacement is spliced across however many runs it spanned — so a mark Word cut into three pieces is still seen and the template's own formatting is untouched. Runs are merged first only for tidiness. (2) The walk covers every paragraph of every part (body, headers, footers, footnotes, tables), which reaches both copies of a text box — the mc:Choice drawing and the mc:Fallback VML — so the two can never disagree on paper; the reference template keeps the date, the number and the signature block in text boxes, and a test asserts each value appears at least twice. (3) The body mark is handled last because it is the only one that changes the document's shape: the words before it stay on the same line («بالإشارة إلى الموضوع أعلاه، …»), further paragraphs become siblings carrying the template paragraph's own alignment and direction, a list item never joins the opening phrase, and the run of blank paragraphs the template leaves underneath is trimmed to one so the closing phrase is not pushed onto a second page. (4) A4 (11906x16838 twips) and A5 (8419x11906) are written into sectPr/pgSz with margins scaled to the paper, and every floating shape is re-anchored from page to margin with its offset shifted by exactly the margin it used to include — A4 output is visually unchanged, A5 keeps the letterhead inside the writing area. Both the DrawingML anchors and the VML fallback styles are rewritten. (5) A mark the letter has no value for is removed rather than left standing; an unknown mark is left exactly as written, because the check on upload already warned about it. Before approval the number reads «مسودة».

Template precedence: the office's own <root>\templates\letter-template.docx (what «فتح قالب المراسلة في Word» writes, then edits in place) > the organisation's template from the setup file, read from the vault via AccountSettingKeys.LetterTemplateDocumentId > the built-in default. The local copy is written temp-then-move so a template is never half written while Word holds it; LetterAr.LocalCopyWarning is the sentence to show beside the button.

Public API the screen packages consume — Wakeel.Core.Services.Correspondence: ITemplateService (GetAsync, CheckAsync, PrepareLocalCopyAsync, SaveLocalCopyAsync, RemoveLocalCopyAsync, LocalCopyPath), ILetterComposer (Compose → docx, RenderHtml → preview and PrintToPdf), ILetterTemplateInspector, IWordAutomation (EditAsync, EditFileAsync), ILetterPdfWriter, ILetterDocumentStore, IBuiltInLetterTemplate; models LetterData, LetterBody/LetterBlock/LetterSpan with LetterBody.Parse for the internal editor's plain form (- bullet, 1. numbered, **bold**), LetterPageSize, LetterMarks (the nine), LetterTemplateCheck (Known/Unknown/Missing/CanCompose), LetterTemplateSource, LetterTemplateOrigin, WordEditResult/WordEditState, and LetterAr for every Arabic sentence. Wakeel.Reports.Letters: LetterComposer, LetterTemplateInspector, BuiltInLetterTemplate, DerivedDocumentBuilder (implements Core's existing IDerivedDocumentBuilder unchanged), LetterDates, LetterHtmlRenderer, LetterPageLayout, WordSession. All of it is registered in App.xaml.cs.

What B3-2 owes this package: an implementation of ILetterDocumentStore over the vault. Register it and TemplateService picks up the setup file's template while DerivedDocumentBuilder starts producing real print copies; without it both fall back safely (built-in template, standalone referral sheet), so no screen is blocked meanwhile.
